summary: Jonathan Lear is a philosopher educated at Yale, Cambridge, Rockefeller University (Ph.D. ~1978), and Western New England Institute for Psychoanalysis. He held appointments at Cambridge, Yale, Clare College, and the University of Chicago (2014–2022).

Jonathan Mark Kenoyer works in Indology and archaeology. He studied at Woodstock School and the University of California, Berkeley (BA ~1974–1983), and was appointed professor of anthropology at the University of Wisconsin-Madison around 1985.

Jonathan Z. Smith was a religious studies scholar educated at Haverford, Yale, and Yale Divinity School. He held posts at Dartmouth, UC Santa Barbara, and the University of Chicago (Dean of the College 1977–1982), and presided over the SBL (2008).

Jong-Nam Choi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at International Buddhist University and the University of Hamburg (PhD 1998) under Lambert Schmithausen, also studying with Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, Albrecht Wezler, and David Seyfort Ruegg.

Jongcheol Lee specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Seoul National University and the University of Tokyo (PhD 1994, under Yasunori Ejima). He held posts at the University of Mysore (1992) and the Academy of Korean Studies (2001).

Jongmyung Kim is a scholar of Buddhist studies, archaeology, and religion. Educated at Yonsei, Seoul National University, and UCLA (MA 1994, supervised by Robert Buswell), he taught Korean Buddhism at the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2012–2019).

Joryu Chiba was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology who studied at Ryukoku University. He held multiple academic posts at Ryukoku University from 1950 to 1989 and directed the Research Institute of Shin Buddhism (1992–1995).

Jos Gommans is a historian and Indologist educated at Radboud University Nijmegen and Leiden University, completing his doctorate under Jan C. Heesterman and André Wink. He was an NWO fellow before becoming associate professor at Leiden in 1993.

Josef Horovitz was a scholar of Central Asian history and archaeology. He earned his doctorate under Eduard Sachau (~1895–1898) and later held a post at Goethe University Frankfurt from around 1914 to 1931.

Josef Schick was an Indologist educated at Tübingen and the University of Berlin (PhD 1889). After posts at Berlin, Bonn, and Heidelberg, he served as full professor at the University of Munich from 1896 to 1925.

Josef Strzygowski was an art historian who studied at the University of Munich (~1883–1885). He held academic posts at the University of Graz (~1892–1909), the University of Vienna (~1909–1933), and Åbo Akademi University.
Josef van Ess was a scholar of religious studies who studied at the University of Bonn (~1953–1959). He held a post at the University of Tübingen from approximately 1968 to 1999.

Joseph Campbell was a religious studies scholar educated at Columbia University, the University of Paris, and the University of Munich. He served as a fellow at Columbia (1927) and taught at Sarah Lawrence College from 1934 to 1972.
Joseph D. Markowski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed a Master of Arts degree at McGill University under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori (attested 2004).

Joseph Dalton Hooker studied at the University of Glasgow (~1832–1839). He worked at the British Geological Survey from 1845 to 1847 and served as Director of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, from 1847 to 1885.

Joseph E. Schwartzberg was a geographer and Indologist educated at Brooklyn College, Maryland, and Wisconsin-Madison (PhD 1960 under Richard Hartshorne). He served as a professor of geography at the University of Minnesota from 1964 to 2000.

Joseph Estlin Carpenter was a scholar of religion, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at University College School and the University of London. He was president of Harris Manchester College and held a post at Oxford (~1889–1915).

Joseph Goldstein is a Buddhist studies teacher educated at Columbia University. After studying with teachers including Anagarika Munindra and Goenka, he taught at Naropa University (1974) and co-founded the Insight Meditation Society and Barre Center for Buddhist Studies.

Joseph Hackin was an archaeologist of Central Asian and Buddhist art. Educated at Paris, Sciences Po, and EPHE under Sylvain Lévi and Louis Finot, he served as conservator at the Musée Guimet and directed DAFA (1934).

Joseph Haroutunian was a scholar of religion and philosophy who studied at AUB, Union Theological Seminary, and Columbia (Ph.D. ~1932). He held posts at Wellesley, McCormick Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (1962–1968).
